terms.meaning: Found by Vasco da Gama, who reached Calicut on 17 May 1498 C.E.
A special pass that let British traders trade without paying tax.
Wars between the English and French in India for political and trade supremacy.
Sole control of a trade. The Portuguese first had it in the eastern trade.

items.name: First and last Europeans in India
items.formula: The Portuguese were both the first to come and the last to leave.
items.example: Their aims: trade monopoly, colonies and spreading Christianity.

items.name: Portuguese governors
items.formula: Francisco de Almeida was the first Viceroy. Albuquerque (1509) took Goa from the Sultan of Vijayapur in 1510.
items.example: Goa stayed their capital; they also held Diu, Daman, Salsette and Hugli.

items.name: Decline of the Portuguese
items.formula: Strong Dutch and English navies, corrupt officials, forced conversions.
items.example: The fall of Vijayanagara hurt their trade.

items.name: Liberation of Goa
items.formula: Portugal stayed after 1947; the Indian Navy drove them out in 1961 C.E.
items.example: Goa, Diu and Daman were their last possessions.

items.name: The Dutch
items.formula: Dutch East India Company, 1602 C.E.; capital Pulicat.
items.example: Centres: Surat, Machalipatnam, Nagapatnam, Cochin. Beaten by the English, they turned to South East Asia.

items.name: The English East India Company
items.formula: Founded in 1600 C.E. with Queen Elizabeth's permission.
items.example: Sir Thomas Roe got trading rights at Surat from Jahangir in 1615; Calcutta was their first capital.

items.name: How the English grew strong
items.formula: Mughal Emperor Farrukh Siyyar gave them dastaks for duty-free trade in Bengal.
items.example: They built forts, hired soldiers and stored arms.

items.name: The French
items.formula: Last to come: French East India Company, 1664; first warehouse at Surat, 1668; capital Pondicherry.
items.example: Governor Dupleix spread French influence in Hyderabad and the Carnatic.

items.name: Decline of the French
items.formula: Little support from France, revolutions at home, a weaker navy than the English.
items.example: Their centres: Pondicherry, Mahe, Karaikal, Chandranagar.

items.name: Order of the East India Companies
items.example: The British company came first, 2 years before the Dutch.

mistakes.text: The Portuguese reached India first, but the first East India Company was the British one (1600).
Capitals: Portuguese Goa, Dutch Pulicat, French Pondicherry, English first Calcutta.
Almeida was the first Portuguese Viceroy; Albuquerque came later and took Goa.
